title: docs: DEVELOPMENT.md's WSL fix installs Node 20 although the daemon needs 22.22+, it seeds the board by hand-editing .moe/ and calls the existing epic/task UI unimplemented, its plugin build runs gradlew from packages/moe-daemon without the proxy, and it still names Gradle 8.10.2, port 3141 and a loopback daemon WSL can reach
description:
Filed by defect hunt #7 (task-44785c82, architect-1dd28c7c). Checked against moe/work-2026-10-24 22348856; detector outputs are in /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-44785c82/B/. Docs-only: edit docs/DEVELOPMENT.md and nothing else.

ITEMS (doc line, then the code or doc line that contradicts it), worst first:
1. :355, the "Node not found" fix, runs `setup_20.x`. But packages/moe-daemon/package.json sets `"engines": { "node": ">=22.22.0" }`, the same doc's :9 says 22.22+/24/26, and TROUBLESHOOTING.md:68-69 says Node 18/20 cannot run the daemon. Use setup_24.x.
2. :144-147 says "The current UI does not create epics or tasks yet … Create epic and task JSON files under `.moe/epics/` and `.moe/tasks/`". :306-310 lists Epic CRUD, task creation, worker status and settings/status bar as "Not yet implemented".
   - All of them exist: moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/toolwindow/{CreateEpicDialog,CreateTaskDialog,WorkerPanel,MoeSettingsDialog}.kt, statusbar/MoeStatusBarWidget.kt, and the plugin.xml:106 action Moe.CreateTask.
   - Hand-writing .moe/ JSON contradicts CLAUDE.md's never-hand-edit rule. Point to the board dialogs or moe.create_epic / moe.create_task.
3. :120-128, "Run the JetBrains Plugin", runs `cd packages/moe-daemon && npm run build` and then `./gradlew runIde` from there.
   - gradlew exists only in moe-jetbrains/.
   - requireBundledAssets in moe-jetbrains/build.gradle.kts:119-135 fails without moe-proxy's dist and node_modules ("Bundled moe-proxy dist not found … Build it first (cd packages/moe-proxy && npm run build)").
   - The same doc's :267-270 block does it right.
4. :361 says "Daemon runs on `127.0.0.1` which WSL can access", and :368 says "The plugin connects to daemon via localhost (works across WSL/Windows boundary)".
   - The default bind is loopback: packages/moe-daemon/src/index.ts:75 `DEFAULT_BIND_HOST = '127.0.0.1'`.
   - WSL agents in NAT mode reach a Windows daemon only when it runs with `--host wsl` / MOE_BIND_HOST=wsl (JetBrains: Agents > Run Agents in WSL), through the WSL gateway (TROUBLESHOOTING.md:183, CLAUDE.md).
   - Measured on this box by hunt #3 (task-ede88939): 127.0.0.1:9876 is refused from WSL (curl rc 7), while the gateway returns 200.
5. :138 says the Gradle wrapper "targets Gradle 8.10.2" and gives regeneration advice with `--gradle-version 8.10.2`. moe-jetbrains/gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.properties pins gradle-9.8.2-bin.zip, so following the advice would downgrade it.
6. :329 says "Port 3141 in use". The default port is 9876 (index.ts:43).
7. :170 says "`-Role` / `--role`: `architect`, `worker`, or `qa`". Both launchers also accept governor: moe-agent.sh:495 checks `^(architect|worker|qa|governor)$`, and moe-agent.ps1 has the same ValidateSet.
8. :426 says "Config location | `MoeSettings`". No such class exists. It is MoeSettingsDialog (toolwindow/MoeSettingsDialog.kt:22), which writes .moe/project.json settings through UPDATE_SETTINGS.
definitionOfDone: `grep -cE 'does not create epics or tasks yet|Task creation UI|Create epic and task JSON files' docs/DEVELOPMENT.md` prints 0.

`grep -cE 'which WSL can access|works across WSL/Windows boundary|`MoeSettings`' docs/DEVELOPMENT.md` prints 0. The -Role line names governor, and the Run-the-JetBrains-Plugin block builds moe-proxy and runs gradlew from moe-jetbrains/. `git diff --name-only` against the merge base lists only docs/DEVELOPMENT.md.

implementationPlan.description:
Edit docs/DEVELOPMENT.md with the session's own editing tool: Edit on a Claude seat, apply_patch on a codex exec seat (both TOOL-witnessed, moe-agent.sh:5237), never Serena or a shell write. This is the governor's wording (comment-ee19c031 on this row, ruling comment-e4b42690 on task-57fe7ad1): this checkout's local .serena/project.yml ignores docs/**, so every Serena editor refuses the file. Docs-only row: no code and no new test file.

The architect's dry-run result is /mnt/d/moe-scratch/plan-b22f/DEVELOPMENT.proposed.md (Windows: D:\moe-scratch\plan-b22f\). DEVELOPMENT.base.md there is the c99801aa doc, so `diff` the two to see every hunk. Read them, but apply the edits with your editing tool; never cp the proposed file into the tree. Line numbers are at c99801aa (the doc is unchanged at cc84c88a); if the file moved, apply by section. Make exactly these edits and nothing else:

1. :355, WSL "Node not found": `setup_20.x` becomes `setup_24.x`, and the lead-in becomes `Install Node.js 24 LTS in WSL separately (the daemon needs 22.22+, 24 or 26):` (engines >=22.22.0).

2a. :144-147, the body of "## Seed Data for the UI" (keep the heading), becomes:
Create epics and tasks through the daemon. Never write `.moe/` files by hand: the daemon is the sole writer of its runtime state.
- JetBrains: **+ Epic** in the board header, **+** in the Backlog column header, or **Tools → Moe → Create Task**.
- VS Code: **Moe: Create Epic** and **Moe: Create Task** in the Command Palette.
- Agents and scripts: `moe.create_epic` and `moe.create_task` (contracts in [MCP_SERVER.md](./MCP_SERVER.md)). From a terminal, with the daemon running: `scripts/moe-call.sh create_epic '{"title":"My epic"}' --project <path>`.

2b. "## Current Feature Coverage": after `- Task detail dialog (approve/reject/reopen)` add
- Epic create, edit and delete (`CreateEpicDialog`, `EpicDetailDialog`) and task creation (`CreateTaskDialog`, also the `Moe.CreateTask` action)
- Worker status (`WorkerPanel`), project settings (`MoeSettingsDialog`), the status bar widget (`MoeStatusBarWidget`) and IDE notifications (`MoeNotificationService`)
Then delete `Not yet implemented (planned):`, its four bullets and the blank line after them. Keep the `See docs/PLUGIN_SPEC.md ...` line.

3. :120-128, "## Run the JetBrains Plugin": replace the `Open moe-jetbrains ... run one of:` line and its code block with:
Build the daemon and the proxy first. The plugin build bundles both, and `requireBundledAssets()` in `moe-jetbrains/build.gradle.kts` fails it when either one's `dist/` is missing or older than its `src/`, or its `node_modules/` is missing. Then run Gradle from `moe-jetbrains/` (or open `moe-jetbrains` in IntelliJ/PyCharm and run the same tasks there):
```bash
cd packages/moe-daemon && npm install && npm run build
cd ../moe-proxy && npm install && npm run build
cd ../../moe-jetbrains
./gradlew runIde     # launches a sandbox IDE
./gradlew buildPlugin
```
On Windows, run `.\gradlew.bat runIde` or `.\gradlew.bat buildPlugin` from `moe-jetbrains\`.
(Keep the one-line `cd … && npm install && npm run build` forms: step 2's check keys on them.)

4a. :361 becomes:
- The daemon binds `127.0.0.1` by default, and WSL in NAT mode cannot reach the Windows loopback. For WSL agents against a Windows daemon, start the daemon with `--host wsl` (or `MOE_BIND_HOST=wsl`): it then also listens on the WSL adapter, and agents reach it through the WSL gateway. In JetBrains on Windows, the **Start Agents** menu toggle **Run Agents in WSL (Linux)** restarts the daemon that way. Mirrored networking uses loopback. See [WSL agents cannot reach the Windows daemon](./TROUBLESHOOTING.md#wsl-agents-cannot-reach-the-windows-daemon).

4b. :368 becomes:
  - The plugin connects to the daemon at `ws://127.0.0.1:<port>/ws`. WSL agents that use a Windows daemon need the `--host wsl` bind described under **Networking**.

5. :138, Gradle note: replace `the committed wrapper targets Gradle 8.10.2.` with `the committed wrapper pins its Gradle version in \`moe-jetbrains/gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.properties\` (\`distributionUrl\`).`. Replace `` `wrapper --gradle-version 8.10.2 --distribution-type bin` flow from `` with `` `wrapper --gradle-version <version> --distribution-type bin` flow (the pinned version, or the one you are moving to) from ``. Name no literal version: one would drift again (the properties file pins 9.8.2 today).

6. :329: `Port 3141 in use` becomes `Port 9876 in use`. The rest of the line is unchanged.

7. :170 becomes `` - `-Role` / `--role`: `architect`, `worker`, `qa`, or `governor` ``.

8. :426, the JetBrains cell `` `MoeSettings` `` becomes `` `MoeSettingsDialog` (writes `.moe/project.json` `settings` through `UPDATE_SETTINGS`) ``. The VS Code cell is unchanged.

Out of scope, leave as is: the partial MCP tool list (:304), the daemon.json field list (:92) and the message-type lists (:408-409).

Error handling: if an old string no longer matches because the file changed after c99801aa, re-read that section and apply the same intent. If a cited UI label or class no longer exists, say so in a task comment and keep the doc to what the code has. Never paper over a mismatch by inventing a name.

Verification: run it once, fresh, from the task worktree root (.worktrees/<taskId>). This docs-only row has no test suite. The mechanical grep gate below is its regression test, and it is how the row meets the epic rail's test requirement.

Run executionContract.checkRefs [0], then [1], joined with ' && '. Submit that exact text, its exit code and the output tail as complete_task's verification.

Do not run the doc's npm or gradlew commands to try them. The shared-checkout rail forbids npm builds, and this gate is the evidence.

[0] covers DoD 1 to 3. It prints `counts: 0 0 0` and then DOC_OK only when all of these hold:
- none of the three DoD grep patterns matches (each `grep -c` is 0);
- the `` - `-Role` / `--role`: `` line names governor;
- inside "## Run the JetBrains Plugin", these lines come in order: a `cd …moe-daemon … npm run build` line, a `cd …moe-proxy … npm run build` line, `cd …moe-jetbrains`, then the first `gradlew runIde|buildPlugin` line.

[1] is DoD 3's scope check against `git merge-base HEAD ${MOE_LAND_TARGET:-moe/work-2026-10-24}`. It prints SCOPE_OK only when no tracked change and no untracked file exists outside docs/DEVELOPMENT.md, and docs/DEVELOPMENT.md itself differs. `.moe/` is excluded because the daemon's board writes land in the control checkout, never in the task worktree.

Error handling for a red check:
- [0] prints the offending line(s), or exits 1 at the role or block check. Fix the doc text, never the check.
- [1] prints `out of scope: <paths>`. Revert those paths, or delete the stray untracked file.
- Re-run both until green.

The architect dry-ran both checks (/mnt/d/moe-scratch/plan-b22f/gate0.txt and gate1.txt):
- [0] failed on the c99801aa doc and passed on the proposed copy.
- Five mutants failed [0]: the role line without governor, no proxy build line, `cd moe-jetbrains` after gradlew, port 3141 restored, and no daemon build line.
- [1] passed with only the doc changed, both uncommitted and committed with MOE_LAND_TARGET set.
- [1] failed on a stray README.md edit, on a stray untracked file and on an unchanged doc.

Adversarial self-review of the doc diff (`git diff $(git merge-base HEAD ${MOE_LAND_TARGET:-moe/work-2026-10-24}) -- docs/DEVELOPMENT.md`). Load the adversarial-self-review skill first.

Checklist:
- Does every changed sentence match the source it rests on (executionContract.sourceAssumptions)? That means: engines >=22.22.0; the JetBrains classes, Moe.CreateTask, the `+ Epic` and `+` labels and the VS Code command titles; requireBundledAssets; DEFAULT_BIND_HOST and DEFAULT_PORT; `--host wsl` and the Run Agents in WSL (Linux) toggle; gradle-wrapper.properties; governor in both launchers; MoeSettingsDialog to UPDATE_SETTINGS.
- Does the text agree with docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md ("Wrong Node.js version" and "WSL agents cannot reach the Windows daemon") and with docs/CONFIGURATION.md (MOE_BIND_HOST and `--host wsl`)? Does the TROUBLESHOOTING anchor resolve to the heading at :181?
- Cross-platform: does the plugin block name the Windows gradlew.bat form, and does the WSL Node line install a 22.22+ line?
- Markdown: are code fences balanced, list items intact, and is the Config location row still 3 cells?
- Was no claim added beyond the 8 items, and no line outside them changed?

If you find something, fix it with step 1's editing tool and re-run step 2's command before complete_task.
